A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SPO and ExtendaBench. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching content moved or redrawn in v4.

before.justification: v3 reports original VirtualHome and Habitat simulation results, component and preference-selection ablations, and comparisons of vision-language models.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds comparator evaluations, diagnostic experiments, dataset analyses, an ALFRED evaluation, and failure cases.

M1.justification: The proposed SPO pipeline retains its scoring dimensions, preference categories, DPO objective, and four-stage curriculum with replay. Appendix B.9 newly specifies selection details, including a 0.1 score margin, without establishing a procedural revision. Alternative evaluators and GRPO appear as experimental variants.

E1.justification: The 1,509-task ExtendaBench coverage across VirtualHome, Habitat, and four difficulty levels is retained. Appendix B.11 adds a limited evaluation on 10% of an ALFRED split. Table 6 also adds descriptive complexity comparisons with ALFRED, LLarp, and the original VirtualHome dataset.

E2.justification: v4 adds InternVL3 8B, single-negative DPO variants, adapted SayCan and ProgPrompt, and GRPO with and without structured preference rewards (Tables 7 and 12–14). These substantially broaden the comparisons. The original six-model comparison is retained as Figure 4, rather than newly introduced.

E3.justification: The original main evaluation settings remain, but v4 adds distinct evaluation designs: a Qwen2.5-VL 3B optimizer comparison on Habitat, instruction-and-image-only controls for SayCan and ProgPrompt, a 10% ALFRED evaluation, and instruction-length and syntactic-complexity metrics. These expand the experimental protocol without establishing that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component and pair-selection ablations, v4 tests evaluator strength, five score-weight combinations, successive curriculum checkpoints, individual negative-selection rules, and structured rewards under GRPO. It also adds action-length versus linguistic-complexity analysis and visual-grounding and history-consistency cases (Appendices A.2 and B.4–B.13).

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Baseline training iterations and curriculum checkpoints are not repeated-run uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the relocated pair-selection results are numerically unchanged. Substantial new results include the GPT-4o evaluator's 49.62% GCR and 19.26% SR, and ALFRED SR of 7.21% for the baseline versus 12.02% for SPO. Under the new 3B Habitat setting, Table 14 reports reward-augmented GRPO at 20.18/16.07 GCR/SR, above SPO's 19.83/14.66; these are additional results, not updates to the original 7B comparison.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 retain the same mathematical content. Appendix A.2 adds intuitive error-accumulation reasoning and empirical complexity statistics, but no new formal assumptions, mathematical definitions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about structured preference optimization, curriculum learning, ExtendaBench, and improved planning. The abstract's numerical improvement claims are unchanged; revised component names clarify existing concepts.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive explanations for direct scoring, evaluator quality, complementary negative categories, task-length difficulty, adapted planners' limitations, and visual/history failures. Some new interpretations overstate the evidence: Section 6.3 claims superiority across all difficulty levels despite counterexamples, and B.10 describes a remaining gap to SPO although Table 14 places reward-augmented GRPO ahead.

D1.justification: Appendix B.9 discloses the 0.1 score margin and additional negative-selection details, while Section D adds a CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 dataset-license statement. Existing sampling, optimization, LoRA settings, and prompts are retained. The v3 disclosure that experiments use one L40 GPU is removed.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations for syntactic-complexity analysis, GRPO/DeepSeekMath, and InternVL3, and sharpens comparisons with general MLLMs, self-improvement methods, Language Rearrangement, and embodied planners. The broad research positioning remains intact. The additional SayCan publication citation represents work already cited in v3.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites refine the abstract, introduction, preference-category descriptions, results discussion, and limitations. The backbone comparison moves into Section 6.2, while the pair-selection discussion moves to Appendix B.3. Terminology, an author affiliation, and acknowledgements are updated, with the main narrative structure largely retained.

P2.justification: v4 substantially expands the diagnostic tables and task/failure illustrations. It replaces v3 Table 6 with radar plots in Figure 4, relocates and enlarges the action distributions as Figure 6, moves the pair-selection table, and restyles main tables. Existing task illustrations are retained alongside additional examples; the radar conversion removes directly tabulated numerical precision.

improvement.justification: v4 supplies useful empirical checks of previously under-tested scoring and negative-selection choices, broader comparator evidence, and concrete failure analysis. These strengthen support for the unchanged method. The net gain is limited by new reporting errors: Appendix A.2.1 attributes Habitat scores to VirtualHome, and B.10 misdescribes the ordering in Table 14. Removing the GPU disclosure and replacing precise backbone scores with radar plots also reduce inspectability.
